# examples/tablePerformance calls a table method the table no longer has

**Claim it first:** comment on this issue before you start, and check the open pull requests for one that already points here. We merge the first approve-worthy PR (see `CONTRIBUTING.md`, point 3). This row comes from #19920, where @bercedev has first pick on its rows.

## Context

Welcome! This is one row of #19920, split out so that its fix closes its own ticket. It is a fix to an example, not to the engine. You need a fork, Node and the dev server (`npm run server-start`); no Agent OS, Docker or AI tooling.

A headless sweep of every example page on 2026-10-20 found `examples/tablePerformance` throwing on load and rendering nothing. It still does on `dev` `f5decee2c0`. Open `http://localhost:8080/examples/tablePerformance/index.html` and the console shows `TypeError: table.createViewData is not a function`. The page fails the same way at `13.2.0`, so this predates 13.3.

## The Problem

`examples/tablePerformance/MainContainer.mjs:146` and `MainContainer2.mjs:146` call `table.createViewData(inputData)` on the table container, which no longer has that method. `MainContainer3.mjs:149` calls it on the table's body (`table.body.createViewData(inputData)`), as the engine's own `src/draggable/table/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs` does.

## The Architectural Reality

- `examples/tablePerformance/Viewport.mjs` mounts all three main containers, so both stale calls run.

## The Fix

The likely fix, which the change confirms: call the method on the table body in both files, as `MainContainer3.mjs` does.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: `examples/tablePerformance` loads with no page error and renders its three tables.
- [ ] AC-2: each table's refresh control fills its table with the requested rows.

## Out of Scope

- The other rows of #19920, which have their own tickets.
- Measuring the table's performance.
